subject: Unexpected 429s affecting BrightDeck inference — post-incident notes and next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodai.com>
To: Ryan Chen <ryan@brightdeck.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected 429s affecting BrightDeck inference — initial mitigation

Hi Ryan —

Thanks for flagging the 429 spikes this morning. We saw a burst of client-side 429s affecting your account between ~07:45–08:10 PT; our runtime reported an aggressive quota check that incorrectly applied a tenant-level burst cap that should not have matched BrightDeck.

Immediate actions we took:
- Temporarily increased your per-minute quota to the expected value to stop further throttles.
- Disabled the new burst-enforcement policy on the affected shard while we investigate.
- Enabled additional logging for keys and routing decisions to capture the misclassification.

We know any interruption during your morning batch-run is costly — apologies. Marcus (cc'd) is owning the technical investigation and will follow up with a root cause and remediation plan. I will send a short post-incident note in the next few hours with timelines and proposed fixes.

Attachments: incident-notation.txt (short log excerpt)

Next steps for you: please confirm whether any queued jobs failed permanently, or if re-submitting is acceptable; if you need us to re-run specific requests, let me know the request IDs.

-Neha

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodai.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected 429s affecting BrightDeck inference — investigation notes

Neha / Evie —

Summary of findings so far (investigation thread):
- Root cause: a recent change to the burst-enforcement aggregation (rolling out 2026-10-13 03:00 UTC) introduced a predicate that incorrectly matched tenant alias patterns when an account used both hosted and dedicated endpoints. BrightDeck’s request routing matched the alias fallback path and was flagged as a shared-tenant traffic pattern.
- Effect: the policy enforced a conservative per-tenant burst cap (180 requests/min) instead of the provisioned 3,600 requests/min for BrightDeck. This produced the 429s.
- Rollback: the policy toggle was disabled at 07:52 PT; temporary quota bump applied at 07:54 PT.

Planned remediation:
1) Revert the predicate and issue a safe config patch (target: 2026-10-14T12:00 PT).
2) Add a targeted unit/regression test for alias fallback matching.
3) Backfill audit logs for affected request IDs and provide a CSV to BrightDeck.
4) Run a scoped deploy to canary and monitor for 24 hours.

I will prepare a short postmortem PDF and a spreadsheet with the affected request IDs for Neha to share. Marcus

---
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodai.com>
To: Ryan Chen <ryan@brightdeck.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodai.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary, timelines, and action items (BrightDeck AI)

Ryan —

Thanks again for the patience this morning. Attached is a short post-incident summary and an action-plan workbook: 'redwood-429-postmortem-20261014.pdf' and 'brightdeck-temporary-quota-increase.xlsx'. Key contents below:

What happened:
- A config change to the burst-enforcement predicate that rolled on 2026-10-13 matched BrightDeck incorrectly under alias-fallback routing, applying a lower burst limit.
- Impact window: 2026-10-14T07:45 PT to 2026-10-14T07:54 PT.
- ~1.2k requests returned 429s; we identified 94 distinct request IDs that were dropped (list in spreadsheet).

What we did:
- Immediate mitigation: disabled the policy and applied a temporary per-minute quota override to your account at 07:54 PT.
- Rollback: predicate reverted and safe patch queued; canary patch target at 12:00 PT (deploy completed at 12:05 PT to canary).
- Customer support: we preserved detailed logs and built a CSV of affected request IDs for reconciliation.

Next steps for Redwood (owner):
- Marcus: release config fix to stable (ETA 2026-10-15 02:00 UTC) and add regression test.
- Engineering: deliver final CSV of affected request IDs and a recommended resubmit plan (ETA 2026-10-14 18:00 PT).
- Product: review change gating to add a secondary alias-pattern regression check for future deployments (owner: Evelyn).

What we ask of BrightDeck:
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to re-run the dropped requests or if you will resubmit. If you want us to re-run, please confirm the request ID list in the attached spreadsheet.
- For audit: please confirm an internal contact for the final CSV delivery (cc'd Ryan).

We are offering a one-time credit for API token costs during the outage window; finance and I can follow up on eligibility if you accept.

Attachments: redwood-429-postmortem-20261014.pdf (postmortem), brightdeck-temporary-quota-increase.xlsx (request IDs + temp quota rows)

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwoodai.com | +1 (415) 555-0173
